name: Fragmentia-AI paper: ULP-WGS cancer vs non-cancer AUC on a held-out validation set, six feature sets x three classifiers
description: Fragmentia-AI trained on ULP-WGS and six re-implemented fragmentomic feature sets, each with random forest, XGBoost and a deep learning classifier, scored on the same held-out ULP-WGS validation set.

attributes.protocol: Feature pipelines for DELFI, Griffin, FRAGMA, FDI, nucleosome and subnucleosome features were re-implemented and applied to the same ULP-WGS training and validation cohorts as Fragmentia-AI; each feature set trained with random forest, XGBoost and deep learning; cancer vs non-cancer AUC on the held-out validation set; p values against Fragmentia-AI.
attributes.version: Fragmentia-AI paper, Table S5 (Document S1); Results P43-P44
limitations: Developer study: Geneseeq employees developed Fragmentia-AI, re-implemented every baseline and ran every arm.
The training/validation split of the ULP-WGS cohort and the number of held-out samples are not stated.
The test behind the printed p values is not named.
Retrospective case-control cohort; AUC only, no sensitivity at a fixed specificity and no tumour-fraction stratum for this comparison.
Results P43 calls the same-platform baseline AUC 0.97 in one sentence and 0.956 in another.

The cohort has 1,245 non-cancer controls, the same number as the training cohort of the Fragmentia-AI WGS paper (Molecular Biomedicine 2026, Table S1) from the same company, so the two studies may share samples; neither paper says.

heldout_validation.note: Split and sample counts not printed
